clue.text: Exaggerate merits of lines at end of love poem

indicators.note: at end of places the lines after the love-and-poem pieces

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, the round letter O
a verse is a poem
LL is the abbreviation for lines, one L per line

explanation.surface: A critic praises the lines closing a love poem far beyond their worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversell something is to talk up its qualities more than they deserve, a synonym for exaggerating its merits.

clue.text: Recalled end of semester — I finished university with a suitable expression?

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the assembled string is taken in the opposite direction
end of picks the closing letter of semester

parts.note: finished means over, as in 'the game is over'

explanation.surface: A student looks back on finishing university at the end of term and wonders what to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns RIOVERUA (R, I, OVER, U, A) round. The definition is cryptic: the French farewell is the fitting thing to say on leaving university.
explanation.definitionFit: This French goodbye is a fitting phrase for someone departing once their studies are finished.

clue.text: Endless cheese and egg providing energy

indicators.note: endless means the cheese loses its final letter

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
an egg is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A snack of cheese and egg gives someone a burst of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or liveliness of style, a synonym for energy.

clue.text: Officers' quarters on ship hosting, say, revolutionary forum

parts.note: the mess is where military officers eat and socialise

indicators.note: hosting means the ship phrase holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: aboard means on a ship

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the abbreviation runs backwards

parts.note: EG (for example) is the abbreviation signalled by say

explanation.surface: Officers' quarters on a warship host a forum for revolutionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: An online message board is a forum where users post and discuss topics.

clue.text: Soccer fans initially anticipating goalless draw

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of fans

parts.note: a goalless draw is a 0-0 tie, written with two O's

explanation.surface: Football fans are expecting a goalless draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anticipating' is a link saying the F comes before the draw. Footie is British slang for football.
explanation.definitionFit: Footie is informal British slang for football, which Americans call soccer.

clue.text: Realised murderer is going round outhouse

indicators.note: going round says the murderer's name encircles the outbuilding

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis, the first murderer
a shed is an outbuilding or outhouse

explanation.surface: A killer is prowling round a garden outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: To cash in is to convert assets into money, a sense of realise in finance.

clue.text: US city, I note, in Washington state

indicators.note: in says the I and note pieces sit inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state
a chit is a short written note or voucher

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a US city lies in Washington state.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is false: the city is in Kansas. 'note' is a chit, not a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Wichita is the largest city in Kansas, in the United States.

clue.text: After outburst of temper, he's given lines

indicators.note: After puts the outburst piece ahead of the pronoun

parts.note: a strop is a bad-tempered sulk or tantrum
he is taken as written; the 's (has) is a link

explanation.surface: After a tantrum, a pupil is given lines as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'given lines' to copy out is a British school punishment, which hides the poetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A strophe is a section of a poem or ode, a group of lines.

clue.text: Oddly great mountain in S Africa, within reach

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of great

parts.note: Table Mountain overlooks Cape Town in South Africa

explanation.surface: An oddly great mountain in South Africa can be reached.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gettable is obtainable, able to be got, so within reach.

clue.text: Take stock: result's unexpected

indicators.note: unexpected suggests the letters of result come out in a surprising order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Doing a stocktake, someone finds the result surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take stock' looks like inventory but means steal livestock; the 's of result's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle is to steal cattle or other livestock, so to take stock in a literal sense.

clue.text: Removal of sticker after exhibition finishes early

indicators.note: after places the sticker following the shortened exhibition
finishes early means the exhibition word stops one letter short

parts.note: a display is an exhibition
cement is something that sticks things together

explanation.surface: A sticker is removed after the exhibition closes early.
explanation.definitionFit: Displacement is the act of moving something out of its place, a synonym for removal.

clue.text: In retirement, daily round a burden?

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: in retirement means going backwards, retreating

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Even in retirement, the daily round can feel like a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid. 'In retirement' turns SUN to NUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a responsibility or obligation, which is a kind of burden.

clue.text: A couple of Liberals intended to depose leader in coalition

parts.note: L stands for Liberal, so two of them are two Ls

indicators.note: to depose leader means the intended loses its first letter

parts.note: your intended is the person you plan to marry, a fiancé

explanation.surface: Two Liberals plan to oust the leader of their coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intended' looks like a verb but is the noun meaning husband-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union of parties for a common purpose, the same as a coalition.

clue.text: Tool one wants repaired

indicators.note: repaired means the letters are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wants a tool repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a small saw used by carpenters for fine joints, a hand tool.

clue.text: Top players in tennis outrivalled, suffering reverse

indicators.note: suffering reverse says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tennis star is beaten and suffers a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the letters held in 'tennis outrivalled'; 'suffering reverse' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuosi are highly skilled performers, especially musicians, the top players in their field.

clue.text: Losing weight, old taxman wears jumper and shirt maybe for work

indicators.note: wears means the taxman is clothed in the other pieces, which go round him

parts.note: a roo (kangaroo) is a jumper
a shirt is an example of a top

indicators.note: losing means the weight letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Matthew the apostle was a tax collector

explanation.surface: A slimmed-down tax inspector puts on a jumper and shirt for the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is a kangaroo, not a sweater. The work is John Braine's 1957 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Room at the Top is a novel by John Braine, a literary work.

clue.text: Area in which one's living

indicators.note: in which says the area word holds the next piece

parts.note: extent means area or size
one is I and the 's is S

explanation.surface: Someone describes the area where they live.
explanation.definitionFit: Existent means existing or alive, synonymous with living.

clue.text: Naturalist identified sound of creature on Noah's craft

indicators.note: sound of says the name is pronounced like these words

parts.note: a lamb is a creature and the ark is Noah's boat

explanation.surface: A naturalist identifies the cry of an animal aboard Noah's ark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noise the creature makes but signals the words heard aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck was a French naturalist known for an early theory of evolution.

clue.text: Renewable energy mostly supported by small political group

indicators.note: in a down clue supported by puts the small piece underneath
renewable is read as able to be made anew, so the letters are reshaped
mostly drops the last letter of energy

explanation.surface: Renewable energy is mostly backed by a small political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renewable energy' looks like a single phrase but 'Renewable' rearranges ENERG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greens are environmentalist political parties, such as the Green Party.

clue.text: Bother! Son overturned drink

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue turns the pieces upside down

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: Bother! A son has knocked over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water or soda pop is a drink.

clue.text: Cardinal in church once abandoning old belief

indicators.note: in places the colour inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is Church of England
cardinal is a deep red colour

indicators.note: abandoning means once loses the old letter

explanation.surface: A cardinal in the church of old abandons an outdated belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman but is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Credence is acceptance that something is true, a synonym for belief.

clue.text: Uninteresting place, such as Swanage or Weston-super-Mare?

definitions.meaning: a dull, small town with little going on
each seaside town's name holds one horse: a nag in Swanage, a mare in Weston-super-Mare

explanation.walkthrough: Swanage and Weston-super-Mare are English seaside resorts; the second sense is a whimsical literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a small, sleepy town lacking interest or amenities.

clue.text: Jester and Lear briefly fought?

parts.note: a wag is a joker or jester

indicators.note: briefly means the last letter of the name is cut off

parts.note: Edward Lear was the Victorian writer of nonsense verse

explanation.surface: A jester and King Lear briefly come to blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' evokes the king with his Fool, but it is the poet Edward Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: To wage war is to carry on fighting, so the phrase means fought.

clue.text: Attacked English teacher after end of period

indicators.note: after places the English teacher behind the period's end

parts.note: the turn of a century or year is the end of that period
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: An English teacher is attacked after the end of a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of period' reads as the last letter of period but means TURN, as in the turn of the century.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on someone is to round on them suddenly, so attacked.

clue.text: Twice drag artist's head lowered for dance

indicators.note: twice means the moved word is doubled
lowered in a down clue moves the letter further down the word

parts.note: to drag is to haul

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the head or first letter of artist is A

explanation.surface: A drag artist's head is twice lowered during a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag artist' looks like a performer but splits: drag is a verb, artist gives its head.
explanation.definitionFit: The hula-hula is the traditional Hawaiian dance, the hula.

clue.text: Young bounder beginning to enjoy time at bar

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise things

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of enjoy

explanation.surface: A young cad starts to enjoy his time at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' suggests a cad, but it is a leaping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare, an animal that bounds.

clue.text: Burgundy wine dry as this, do you say?

indicators.note: do you say asks whether the word is pronounced like this

parts.note: the idiom is dry as a bone

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Burgundy wine is as dry as the speaker says.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaune is a town in Burgundy whose name is given to its red and white wines.

clue.text: Note pre-decimal currency no longer on the market?

parts.note: sol (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
D stood for the penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A banknote of pre-decimal currency is no longer traded.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money was pounds, shillings and pence, with d for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sold has been bought and so is no longer available for sale.
